mechanism_card.hypothesis: A small subset of R0 dots is displaced from shallow magnetic-source edges; a decisive vertical-gradient gain can re-centre those dots without the wholesale movement and spacing loss of earlier SNAP recipes.
mechanism_card.mechanism: Response = footprint percentile of abs(tmi_vg). Only a dot whose Euclidean <=2 px window contains a currently admissible destination at least 0.10 response percentile higher can move. Proposals are gain-ordered; every destination must be in-footprint, off-catalogue, at least 3 px from the catalogue, finite, and no closer than 2.8 px to another final dot. R0's inherited sub-3 px pixels remain fixed. Unit mass and 37,654-dot count are unchanged, so this is a position experiment rather than MASS, PRUNE or CONCENTRATION.
mechanism_card.non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Vertical derivatives also amplify shallow dikes, volcanic or lithologic contacts, cultural ferrous sources and gridding noise; a dipping contact's gradient maximum need not coincide with its surface fault trace.
mechanism_card.predicted_live_change: +0.001 DTI (MODEL; plausible interval -0.010 to +0.010; not a score)
mechanism_card.falsifier: A paired live receipt Δ<=-0.010 versus R0 falsifies the positive magnetic re-centring hypothesis; |Δ|<0.010 is no evidence.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: A vertical-derivative maximum is a potential-field source-edge locator, not direct evidence of brittle faulting. Review relocated dots against mapped geology, dipping contacts and non-fault shallow sources before interpreting any receipt.
